stewart_read: No company name, no lead source, no reason for calling in the opening line — the customer is left to ask if the rep even has the right number.
coaching_implication: Open with 'Hey, this is Randy with ION Solar, following up on the solar request for this address' before anything else — legitimacy has to land before the first customer question.

quote: Tell me what your program is like.
stewart_read: Rep answers with a full bill-swap/no-upfront-cost pitch before any qualification, which is closer-tier persuasion content offered unprompted by the flow.
alternative_hypothesis: Strategic read: customer demanded it directly, so some answer was unavoidable — but the rep could have kept it to one line and redirected faster.
coaching_implication: A short one-line framing plus immediate redirect to verify would have kept scope tighter: 'It's a bill-swap program — let me grab a few details and I can show you exactly how it applies to your home.'

quote: But what is your job? Just to get appointment?
stewart_read: This is effectively a legitimacy/trust objection dressed as a curiosity question; the rep answers literally instead of using it to build value in the appointment itself.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive read is more supported — the rep gives a flat, accurate answer with no reframe, missing a chance to plant curiosity about the design's savings number.
coaching_implication: Could reframe: 'My job is to get you the real numbers on paper so the specialist isn't wasting your time — that part's on me.'

quote: Okay. So what do you want me to do right now?
stewart_read: The customer hands the rep a clean opening to reset the frame and build curiosity about his own savings; rep instead moves straight into administrative verify questions.
coaching_implication: Rep could have said something like 'Let's find out what your specific numbers look like' before diving into address/roof questions — ties the verify section to a payoff.

stewart_read: Bill amount is captured but immediately followed by a flat acknowledgement and the next script question — no flip into alignment-against-the-utility.
coaching_implication: Flip line was available here: 'So over $300 a month to the utility — that's exactly what this program is built to replace.' Never delivered.

quote: Alright. I gotta go. I'm right in the middle of work right now.
stewart_read: Customer signals urgency to end the call mid bill-collection; rep pushes forward for the email one more time instead of adapting pace, adding friction right before the close.
alternative_hypothesis: Strategic read doesn't hold — there's no evidence the rep is deliberately slowing down; this reads as simple lack of pacing awareness under time pressure.
coaching_implication: Acknowledge the time crunch explicitly ('I know you're at work, let's wrap this in one minute') to reduce irritation before locking the appointment.

quote: Oh, man. You're gonna be a salesperson. You gotta do better than that, man.
stewart_read: Live fumbling with the scheduling tool during the close visibly damages the customer's confidence right as the appointment is being locked in.
coaching_implication: Have available times ready before offering to check the calendar live — dead air while searching invites exactly this kind of mockery at the worst moment.
